page.layout: One printed page. Top: running head with page number at top right; four lines of verse at full width. Then a division heading (CL. V. CALLARTIO I. C., Aurelienfi) with an italic poem of verse stanzas. Below a rule: a heading "In viros, more turpissimo, γυναικο-κομῶν" and a further verse stanza.

main_text.p: Sublimem properans ad Sfque Sinam, Et diua iuga sacra Cattarina: Quid profecerit hoc labore quaeris? Res natos reperit domum reuersus.
main_text.head: CL. V. CALLARTIO I. C. Aurelienfi.

p.i: EN senos tibi mitto pippiones, Ruris munera rustica nostri, Nostri non penitus tamen, sed olim Futuri, nisi forte me fefellit Patronus mea iura qui tuetur: Iura tanta quidem, ut nec his ferendis Terga sufficiant onusta muli. Hos ergo tibi mitto pippiones. Obtestorque Deum simul, beato Ut senis tibi mesibus peractis, Fas sit coniuge de tua pudica, Tot natos numerare Sagientes, Quot fetus tibi mitto pippientes.

main_text.head: In viros, more turpissimo, γυναικο-κομῶν τῶς.

p.i: Incinnatulus ille, cui Sndulati, Propexique humeros grauant capilli, Qui terfa cute, blafulaque voce, Qui patis oculis, gradúque molli,

page.notes: Printed page with a rule dividing the verse; the Greek heading "γυναικοκομῶν" is partly garbled in the scan, and the spelling "Sfque", "Sinam", "Sndulati" and "pippiones" are as printed. Mixed long s and f forms are normalised to s.
